comments.body: https://github.com/Pr0methean/rust_rdrand/tree/578e2c7a4375a39bbbbfe0e42088a58bf5e23f2c is a version that compiles and runs fine on x86_64 but still triggers SIGSEGV on aarch64.

This is just an LLVM assertion that fired. With `-Zverify-llvm-ir` you get

```
Intrinsic has incorrect return type!
ptr @llvm.aarch64.rndrrs
rustc-LLVM ERROR: Broken module found, compilation aborted!
```

It is expected that LLVM assertions cause a crash without any message. We compile LLVM with `-DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=OFF -DLLVM_UNREACHABLE_OPTIMIZE=OFF` which causes LLVM to turn every assertion into a trap, which in some cases is implemented as writing to an unmapped address: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/57f1ec6e0a4ec3cd4a485ca1ec85e3efe541933b/llvm/include/llvm/Support/Compiler.h#L488-L500 In addition it is very much expected that abusing LLVM intrinsics causes crashes when the LLVM IR verifier is disabled (as we do for perf reasons)

Your signature for that intrinsic is incorrect, based on the llvm test here 

https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/9cc615a2f5cfbdd28dc835758c35c12cba65e61f/llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/rand.ll#L22-L40

It should be 

```
declare { i64, i1 } @llvm.aarch64.rndrrs()
```

LLVM will segfault when you use an intrinsic with an incorrect type. 

---

Probably `rust-lang/stdarch` should wrap this intrinsic? Looks like it might be new in LLVM 22?
Does that translate to `fn rndrrs() -> (i64, bool)` in Rust, or to what?

For now this seems to work?

https://godbolt.org/z/41z84v18f

It might or it might not. Not all LLVM intrinsics can be called in Rust. For some there is no way to convince cg_llvm to lower Rust types to the right LLVM function signature. (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/140763 helps with that for a couple of types, but definitively not all) You will have to try. In any case, do note that the ability to call LLVM intrinsics is unstable and your ability to call any particular LLVM intrinsic may break without replacement in any future rustc version (in addition to the fact that LLVM occasionally changes LLVM intrinsics). `link_llvm_intrinsics` is effectively an implementation detail of stdarch. The `internal_features` lint triggers on it for a reason. If anything I would recommend using inline asm rather than an LLVM intrinsics for rndrrs.
Looks like adding it to `stdarch` is straightforward https://github.com/rust-lang/stdarch/pull/2050.
Closing as this is not-a-bug -- internal features are labeled "internal" for a reason. They should not be used outside this repository.

title: SIGSEGV in rustc when using #[link_name = "llvm.aarch64.rndrrs"]
